# M2-2: MCP server in serve

- Milestone: M2
- Branch / worktree: `t/M2-2`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M2-2`
- Depends on: M2-1b
- Touches (exclusive while running): mcp/ (new), cmd/, config/, .env.example, go.mod, go.sum
- Plan refs: §4 (all), N6, N7, R9. Spike: `spikes/mcp/{main,mcpserver}.go`.
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (the endpoint stays dark until M2-5)

## Goal
`finbot serve` runs an authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP server beside the scheduler, with the first read tool. Tools read
SQLite only and never call YNAB, so they can't touch the rate budget.

## Scope
- `mcp/`: go-sdk v1.8.0, resource-server auth using the `auth/` verifier. `tools/list` is limited by the caller's token.
- Set the protected-resource metadata `ResourceName` to exactly `finbot` (the spike says `finbot (spike)`). M2-5 uses this to prove traffic left the spike.
- Mount the AS with `mux.Handle("/oauth/", srv)` and `mux.Handle("/.well-known/", srv)`. Set `RequireBearerTokenOptions.Scopes` to `[]string{auth.ScopeMCP}`, because `VerifyToken` doesn't check scope itself.
- Port the spike's `cors` and `logRequests` middleware from `spikes/mcp/main.go`. Browser clients need `cors`. Logs stay free of tokens, emails and ids.
- Tool registration: one slice in `mcp/`, with each tools file adding itself, so later tasks only add files.
- Tool `data_freshness`. A shared response helper puts data freshness in every tool response (§4).
- Config: `MCP_LISTEN_ADDR` (default `:8080`), `MCP_PUBLIC_URL`, `MCP_DATA_DIR` only if still needed,
  `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MCP_ALLOWED_EMAILS`. MCP is disabled unless all the required
  values are set, so existing deploys and local runs keep working.
- **Health stays private.** The tunnel forwards every path on the MCP port to the public internet, and `/healthz` returns
  `last_error`. Serve it on its own listener: `HTTP_ADDR` default becomes `127.0.0.1:8081`, and the MCP port must return
  404 for `/healthz`. `finbot health` keeps working from inside the container, and `cmd/probe.go`'s default moves to match.
- `finbot revoke <email | u_hash | --all>`: one-step revocation via `RevokeUser`, no restart. The hash form means no email needs to be on argv in a container exec. It opens only `FINBOT_DB_PATH` and needs no YNAB or Google env.
- Add `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` to `secrets(cfg)` in `cmd/app.go`.
- Run `auth.Prune` at startup and daily, on the scheduler's goroutine, logging its outcome. A failure must not fail the sync.
- Graceful shutdown covers the new listener. Logs carry no tokens, emails or ids.
- If finbot logs client IPs, use `CF-Connecting-IP` only as §4 allows.

## Out of scope
- Other tools (M2-3, M2-4), compose, tunnel and deploy.sh (M2-5), write tools (M5).

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Test: `/mcp` without a token returns 401 with resource metadata; with a valid token `tools/list` and
      `data_freshness` work; with a revoked token returns 401.
- [ ] Test: a request with the public Host on the `:8080` listener isn't refused by the DNS-rebinding guard.
- [ ] Test: `/healthz` is 404 on the MCP listener and works on `HTTP_ADDR`; `finbot health` exits 0.
- [ ] Test: serve with MCP config blank behaves as today (sync, status and backup jobs run, no MCP listener).
- [ ] Test: `finbot revoke` works with only `FINBOT_DB_PATH` set.
- [ ] Test: the protected-resource metadata has `ResourceName` `finbot`.
- [ ] Test: `Prune` runs at startup and on its tick, and a Prune error doesn't mark sync unhealthy.
- [ ] Test: a token without the MCP scope is refused on `/mcp`; a browser preflight gets the CORS headers.
- [ ] Test: SIGTERM closes both listeners and the DB.
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `mcp/` (new): `NewHandler` (Streamable HTTP behind `RequireBearerToken`, `Scopes: [auth.ScopeMCP]`, one shared server). `tools.go`: the `registry` slice, `register` called from each tools file's `init`, and the `Response[T]` wrapper that adds freshness to every tool. `freshness.go`: `data_freshness`. `middleware.go`: `CORS`, `LogRequests`.
  - `tools/list` and `tools/call` are limited per request by `limitToToken`, using that request's token. A refused tool gets the same error as a tool that doesn't exist.
  - `cmd/mcp.go`: `startMCP` (own listener, only `/mcp`, `/oauth/`, `/.well-known/`) and `addPrune` (startup and daily, on the scheduler goroutine). `cmd/revoke.go`: `finbot revoke`. `cmd/app.go`: `serve` runs both listeners, `shutdown` drains then force-closes, `secrets` adds the Google secret and allowlisted emails. `cmd/scheduler.go`: the prune job.
  - `config/`: `MCP` settings, `Missing`, `LoadDBPath`, `DefaultHTTPAddr` = `127.0.0.1:8081`, which `cmd/probe.go` shares. `.env.example` updated.
- Acceptance (all in `go test ./cmd ./mcp ./config`; `-race` also passes):
  - `/mcp` no token → 401 with metadata; valid token → `tools/list` and `data_freshness` work; revoked → 401: pass, `TestServe_MCPEndToEnd` (real listeners, real auth server, full DCR/consent/token flow against a fake Google).
  - Public Host not refused by the rebinding guard: pass, `TestDNSRebindingGuard` (container address → 200, loopback → 403, which proves the guard is on), and `TestServe_MCPEndToEnd` over a real non-loopback socket (it logs and skips that part on a host with no such interface; it ran here).
  - `/healthz` 404 on the MCP listener, works on `HTTP_ADDR`, `finbot health` exits 0: pass, `TestServe_MCPEndToEnd`, `TestProbe_DefaultMatchesServe` (this one skips if 8081 is busy).
  - MCP blank behaves as today: pass, `TestServe_MCPBlankBehavesAsToday`, `TestServe_MCPBlankKeepsStatusAndBackup`. Sync and the Slack status actually run. The backup job is only checked as armed (`sched.Backup` set); it doesn't fire, because it's nightly.
  - `finbot revoke` with only `FINBOT_DB_PATH`: pass, `TestRevoke_OnlyNeedsDBPath`, plus a built-binary run under `env -i` for the two refusal paths.
  - `ResourceName` `finbot`: pass, `TestServe_MCPEndToEnd`.
  - Prune at startup and on its tick, error doesn't mark sync unhealthy: pass, `TestScheduler_PruneRunsAtStartupAndOnItsTick`, `TestScheduler_PruneErrorLeavesSyncHealthy`, `TestAddPrune`.
  - Token without the MCP scope refused (403), preflight gets CORS headers: pass, `TestAuthOnEndpoint`, `TestCORS`, `TestServe_MCPEndToEnd`.
  - SIGTERM closes both listeners and the DB: pass, `TestServe_SIGTERMClosesListenersAndDB` (real signal through `Main`, with a client stream open). The DB close is shown indirectly: the `-wal` file is gone. `TestShutdown_EndsOpenStreams` covers the forced close.
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`: pass.
  - Mutation check: 32 distinct mutations of the security checks and related behavior, counting only test failures as kills (5 first-pass "kills" were compile errors and were redone as mutations that compile). 29 killed. 3 survived: a `/healthz` route on the inner mux, which is unreachable; the email scrub on `revoke` errors, which never contain the email; and a startup prune error reaching `Health`, which the first sync overwrites. Two real gaps it found are fixed and now tested (the forced `Close`, and a prune-tick error reaching `Health`).
  - Not exercised: real Google, real Cloudflare and the real compose network. The first run against them is M2-5.
- Deviations from brief:
  - `finbot revoke` calls `Storage.BumpGeneration`, not `Server.RevokeUser`. `RevokeUser` is a one-line wrapper over it, but building a `Server` needs an identity provider, and revoke must not need Google env.
  - `MCP_DATA_DIR` isn't added: everything is in SQLite.
  - Added beyond the brief:
    - `revoke` refuses anything that isn't an email, a whole `u_` hash or `--all`, and refuses a missing database file. Either would otherwise report success with every token still valid.
    - Google discovery failing at startup doesn't stop serve: MCP routes answer 503 and it retries every 30 s while sync keeps running. A port conflict still fails serve at once, before any job runs.
    - `MCP_PUBLIC_URL` is validated in config (bare https origin, http only on loopback), so a typo fails at startup.
    - Stray request paths are logged as `other`, since they're attacker-chosen text. Client IPs aren't logged, so `CF-Connecting-IP` isn't read.
    - Tool failures reach the client as a generic message; the detail goes to the log, redacted.
- Follow-ups for backlog:
  - M2-3/M2-4: add a tool with `register(auth.ScopeMCP, &sdkmcp.Tool{...}, handler)` from an `init` in a new file. The handler returns only its data. There's no way yet to send a client a specific error (such as a bad filter), so the first tool needing one should add it next to `errTool`.
  - Later: R11a's Slack side. `status/` flags only `in_error`; it doesn't use the 14-day rule, so an account with a stale import reads `links_ok: false` in MCP answers but leaves the Slack status green.
  - M2-5: `deploy.sh` must forward `MCP_*` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_*`. An open MCP client stream makes shutdown take the full 5 s, which fits Docker's 10 s stop grace.
- Docs follow-ups:
  - CLAUDE.md: add the `mcp/` package role and the `finbot revoke` command; `HTTP_ADDR` default is now `127.0.0.1:8081`; add the `MCP_*` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_*` config (add them to the "forwarded by deploy.sh" list in M2-5); note the prune job in the `Scheduler` paragraph; `/healthz` is on its own private listener.
  - README.md: `/healthz` line and the `finbot revoke` command.
  - Local `.env` files copied from the old example with `HTTP_ADDR=:8080` will now collide with `MCP_LISTEN_ADDR` when MCP is on; serve fails at startup with "address already in use". Remove that line.

## Review fixes (agy FIX, `../_reviews/M2-2.md`)
- Finding 1 (per-account freshness), fixed in `mcp/freshness.go`. The shared helper now puts this in every tool response, through the `register` wrapper:
  - `accounts`: each open bank-linked account of the active plan, by name, never id: `status` (`ok`, `link_error`, `no_recent_import`, `never_imported`), `in_error`, `last_import_date`, `import_age_days`, `last_import_seen_at`.
  - `links_ok`: false if any linked account needs attention, separately from the sync's `stale`. So a fresh sync with a broken link reads `stale: false, links_ok: false`.
  - `warnings`: plain sentences naming each problem account, plus a stale or never-run sync.
  - It reuses `Syncer.Freshness` (`sync/mirror.go`) on a syncer with no YNAB client, so there's no new query and tools still can't call YNAB.
- Limits to know about:
  - R11a's N is left open by the plan, so `importStaleAfterDays` = 14 is my choice, from healthy live links last importing 1-12 days ago (spike F6). It's a constant, and easy to change. A quiet but healthy account past 14 days is flagged, and the warning says it may just have had no activity. On the live plan, expect `links_ok: false` from day one, because 3 cards are in error.
  - `last_import_seen_at` is only an upper bound until an import arrives after the first full load, because those rows all carry the load's time. The field's schema description says so, and no status depends on it.
- `finbot revoke` on a well-formed typo, done. It now counts live tokens first through the new `Storage.ActiveTokens` (unexpired, not rotated or used, current generation; access, refresh and unredeemed codes) and says one of:
  - `revoked N active tokens for u_x`
  - `no active tokens for u_x, so nobody was signed out. If you expected some, check for a typo.`, or the `--all` equivalent
  - `revoked tokens for u_x (couldn't count them)`, if the count fails

  Exit stays 0 in all three. The generation is still bumped with no tokens, because a sign-in waiting on the consent page holds none yet and must still be cancelled. A failed bump exits 1. This can't tell a typo from a real user who has no tokens, which is why it says "if you expected some".
- Deviation: `ActiveTokens` is in `auth/storage.go`, outside this brief's Touches list, because it reads `auth`'s tables and JSON. It's one new read-only method; no existing code in `auth/` changed.
- Tests: `TestFreshness_BrokenLinksShowWhenSyncIsFresh` (healthy, 14 and 15 days, in error, never imported, only a deleted import, manual entry, unlinked, closed, deleted, other plan), `TestFreshness_AllHealthy`, `TestFreshness_StaleSyncWarns`, `TestEveryToolResponseCarriesAccountFreshness` (a non-`data_freshness` tool, and no ids on the wire), `TestDaysSince_UsesCalendarDaysInNowsZone`, `TestActiveTokens`, `TestRevoke_FailuresAreNotReportedAsNoTokens`. `TestServe_MCPEndToEnd` runs real, typo and repeat revokes against tokens from the real flow.
- Checks: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` pass, and `-race` passes on `mcp`, `auth`, `cmd`. Mutation check on the new code: 19 valid mutations, all killed. Two survived the first pass and led to the new rotation and failure-path tests.
- Not exercised: the live plan's accounts. The test data is seeded, with shapes from the mirror schema.
- Docs follow-ups, added to the list above: CLAUDE.md's `auth/` role can mention `ActiveTokens`; document the `data_freshness` fields and the 14-day rule wherever the MCP tools get written up.
